What does it cost to install carpet in Duvall, WA?

Most of what we recarpet in Duvall is a subdivision house trading builder-grade for something that lasts, and that work runs $4 to $7 per square foot installed — the carpet, the pad, labor, new tack strip and the haul-away all inside that figure. Whole projects usually total $2,000 to $4,500. Add a staircase to a 1,200 sq ft main floor and expect $5,500 to $8,500. Grade decides most of the spread, and you settle grade on your own floor.

What does carpet stretching cost in Duvall?

Ripples show up first in hallways and family rooms, the straight runs a builder plan gets walked down most, and they don't mean the carpet is finished. A power stretcher takes waves, buckles and rippling back out for about a fifth of the cost of replacing the floor — $99 per room to start in Duvall. Whenever the pile still stands and you can live with the color, that's the smarter money.
What does it cost to carpet stairs in Duvall?

Stairs start at $18 per step, done either waterfall or cap-and-band. Landings and pie-shaped winders are measured and written into the quote from the start, so the stair figure you approve is exactly what you pay — nothing gets tacked on after the fact.
How long does a carpet install take?

One working day covers most Duvall installs. A typical uphill two-story — three or four bedrooms plus the staircase — is a standard day for our crew. A large house with stairs and heavy furniture throughout can carry into a second day, and the timeline is spelled out on your written quote.
Do you move furniture, or do I clear the rooms?

We move it. Beds, dressers, couches and tables are included on most jobs, and the crew sets everything back where it started. Your part is the small stuff — empty the closets and pack up electronics, breakables and anything you'd rather carry yourself.
Is my carpet worth restretching, or is it time to replace?

Four things push a floor past saving: traffic lanes crushed flat, seams letting go, backing gone brittle, and pet odor that outlived a professional cleaning — that last one settles a lot of Duvall houses, mud and dogs being what they are. Short of those, with the pile upright, the backing sound and the color still fine, it's a $99-per-room stretch rather than a new floor. We look first, then tell you which one you have.

What's the best carpet for a house with dogs?

Start with the pad: a moisture barrier is what keeps an accident from reaching the subfloor, which is where odor turns permanent. Over it goes solution-dyed nylon with a sealed backing — dye that runs through the fiber, so a spot can take diluted bleach and keep its color. In a valley town with a long mud season and plenty of dogs, that pairing pays off. That barrier pad starts at $0.65 per square foot.
What warranty do I get on the install?

Two documents, both printed on your quote. The mill's covers the carpet — wear and stain, 10 to 25 years depending on grade. OC Flooring's covers the labor: a 1-year workmanship warranty on seams, stretch and the staircase, which in most Duvall two-stories is the hardest-working part of the job. The catch is that some mills void coverage under the wrong pad, so all three pad grades come in the van and one gets matched to the carpet you pick.
